Hi Serdar (and ggplot people at large, just joined the list...)

I don't think ggplot has anything to calculate ACF/PACF but that's ok,
you can calculate the values with R and plot them with ggplot:

#lh is an example dataset which is a time series
#?acf should let you decide how to handle your data

d <- acf(lh, plot=FALSE)
df <- data.frame(d$lag, d$acf)
p <- ggplot(df, aes(d.lag, d.acf))
p + geom_bar(stat='identity')

I don't know how to make the bars as skinny as ACF plots usually are,
I tought geom_bar(width=....) would do the trick but it doesn't appear
to...

Hope that helps,
David

JiHO said:

For some reason, widths needs to be in a aes call currently.

p + geom_bar(stat='identity', aes(width=0.2))

see:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/8dd1879200b88e5f/8936478a77ec5a96?lnk=gst&q=Standard+deviation+and+stacked+barcharts#8936478a77ec5a96
